title: Level With Me
logline: The Hardwicks are cursed with chaos: storms find them, fires find them, and the six of them have never once agreed on anything. In the backyard, Hank is building a dome, and every time the family breaks, the dome becomes something new.
genre: Hyper-drama with a slight comedy: the stakes are real and the tears are real, the jokes land between them.
tone: Big feelings, fast turns, hard cuts. A scene can start as a fight and end as a confession. Comedy comes from character, never from the scene stopping for a gag. Hank's thought spirals and Cody's visions are scenes of their own, in their own look and sound.

writers_room.never_on_screen: These are the undercurrents. No character ever says them out loud.
themes: A geodesic dome is the code version of a house: it is a program. Change one number and it is a different building. Every episode the family 'reprograms' it into what they need: a frame, a server room, a toddler's toy, a stage, a lab, a refuge.

Because it is programmable, the dome is the perfect teaching vessel: a toddler builds one from straws, a teenager learns a mitre saw, a coder learns loops from it, a girl plays house in it. It is the stem cell of projects.
Hank is raising boys into men, and quietly every boy who comes near him. It is never named. We see it in what he lets them try, what he makes them fix, and when he says nothing.
The family is cursed with chaos and misfortune, and they joke about it. The joke turns out to be true, and the curse turns out to be the thing that keeps pushing them forward.
Some of them are trying to leave and some are trying to hold everyone together. The one thing all six agree on is that they will never all agree on anything.
rules: Every episode reprograms the dome once, and the new program solves (or causes) the episode's crisis.

Every episode carries one hidden lesson that a viewer could learn from the dome without being told: triangles share the load, frequency is resolution, a jig makes a hundred things the same, a seam is a promise between two panels.
Every figure about the dome comes from the model, spoken through {tokens}.
Anna is left out of at least one family-together moment per episode, and somebody notices only later.
Hank gets one thought spiral per episode at most. Cody gets one vision at most. They are earned, not decoration.

hank.name: Hank Hardwick
hank.role: dad; host of Hank's Hardware Hour
hank.quirk: Thinks permutationally: many angles at once. His speech stops and starts, races, stutters, sometimes makes no sense at all, and the thought spirals become scenes of their own.
hank.secret: A genius everyone takes for a goof. Loves teaching. Steers boys into men without ever saying so.

krystal.name: Krystal Hardwick
krystal.quirk: Silly, playful, the first to laugh, until she puts her foot down. When she does, she takes the head-of-the-house role completely, and everyone, Hank included, falls in line.

anna.name: Anna Hardwick
anna.quirk: Long princess hair, happy-go-lucky, chill, a bit of an airhead. The spearhead of the kids, always off doing her own thing for them, and so always missing the moments when the family is together.

maya.name: Maya Hardwick
maya.quirk: Tough, all attitude. She side-eyes people and cannot hide it, and her mouth gets her into trouble.

cody.name: Cody Hardwick
cody.quirk: Aloof, sometimes clueless about what is right in front of him, and he has visions: sudden flashes of something that has not happened yet.

jet.name: Jet Hardwick
jet.quirk: Keeps piercing his own ear and letting it close up. Hides the earring from his parents and wears it everywhere else. A paranoid, brilliant hustler in the making: burner phones, schemes, a bunker mentality at sixteen.

dale.name: Dale Plumb
dale.quirk: Sarcastic, can't stand the new generation, lives like the party never ended. Busts everyone's chops, most of all Hank's, and would take a bullet for him.

dusty.name: Dusty Vance
dusty.role: peaked in high school; still the cool guy
dusty.quirk: Letterman jacket, a car he can't afford, a story about the state semi-final. Charming, empty, and somehow always around.

yarrow.name: Mr. Yarrow
yarrow.quirk: Says the true thing nobody wants to hear, then goes back to his roses.
